title: "Pseudoword spelling analysis"
output: html_document
date: "2026-08-07"

## Object naming guide

Objects describe the contents and level of each dataset:

- `spelling_responses_wide`: imported participant response columns.
- `spelling_trials`: one row per participant and stimulus, with Toolkit measures.
- `spelling_accuracy_trials`: trials with Toolkit and sample-based accuracy scores.
- `spelling_accuracy_standardized`: accuracy trials with standardized predictors.
- `spelling_agreement_trials`: trials with reading groups and item-group entropy.
- `participant_spelling_summary`: participant-level averages for legal mappings.
- `participant_spelling_summary_zero_coded`: participant averages with missing
  Toolkit values coded as zero, following the original analysis.
- `cumulative_accuracy_trials`: trials with cumulative sample accuracy thresholds.

`model_` names identify the outcome, grain size, predictor or scoring definition.
`plot_` names identify figures. `pg` means phonographeme and `or` means onset-rime.
`consistency` replaces the ambiguous `prob` shorthand for Toolkit measures.
Original workbook column names and exported figure filenames are retained.

## Import data and configure dependencies

```{r}
library(openxlsx)
library(readxl)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(stringi)
library(ggplot2)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(corrplot)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(patchwork)
library(purrr)

# Run with the repository folder as the working directory.
# Override these paths with Sys.setenv(...) when files are stored elsewhere.
data_path <- Sys.getenv("NTR_DATA_PATH", "ntr_pw_spell_data_final.xlsx")
toolkit_path <- Sys.getenv("NTR_TOOLKIT_PATH", "toolkit/Toolkit_v2.0.RData")
converter_path <- Sys.getenv("NTR_CONVERTER_PATH", "toolkit/Transcription_Converter.R")

if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  stop("Workbook not found: ", data_path,
       ". Set the working directory to the repository or set NTR_DATA_PATH.")
}
required_sheets <- c("Spellings", "Demographics")
missing_sheets <- setdiff(required_sheets, readxl::excel_sheets(data_path))
if (length(missing_sheets)) {
  stop("Missing workbook sheets: ", paste(missing_sheets, collapse = ", "))
}

# Toolkit data and converter are external dependencies, not included here.
for (path in c(toolkit_path, converter_path)) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Required external file not found: ", path)
}
load(toolkit_path)
source(converter_path)

# Transcriptions
spelling_responses_wide <- read_excel(
  data_path, sheet = "Spellings") %>% mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ .x %>% str_to_lower() %>% str_replace_all("\\s+", ""))) %>%
  mutate(inhouse = map_chr(pronunciation, ipa_to_inhouse), .after = pronunciation) %>%
  mutate(length = str_length(inhouse), .after = inhouse)

spelling_trials <- spelling_responses_wide %>% pivot_longer(cols = -c(target_spelling, pronunciation, inhouse, length), names_to = "ID", values_to = "spelling_response")

# Read demographics sheet
demographics <- read_excel(data_path, sheet = "Demographics")

# Verify the participant join rather than silently accepting duplicate/missing IDs.
required_demo_columns <- c("ID", "Age", "Sex", "Education", "WRMT_WID",
                           "WRMT_WA", "WRMT_BSC", "WJTA_SPELL")
missing_columns <- setdiff(required_demo_columns, names(demographics))
if (length(missing_columns)) {
  stop("Missing demographic columns: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
}
if (anyNA(demographics$ID) || anyDuplicated(demographics$ID)) {
  stop("Demographic IDs must be nonmissing and unique.")
}
response_ids <- unique(spelling_trials$ID)
missing_ids <- setdiff(response_ids, demographics$ID)
if (length(missing_ids)) {
  stop("Participants without demographic records: ", paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "))
}
# Retain the response sample; extra demographic rows do not add participants.
spelling_trials <- spelling_trials %>%
  left_join(demographics, by = "ID", relationship = "many-to-one")

message("Imported ", length(response_ids), " participants from ", data_path)
# Preserve missing covariates; do not impute values or recode them as zero.
missing_covariates <- spelling_trials %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(across(c(Age, Education, WRMT_WID, WRMT_WA, WJTA_SPELL),
                   ~ sum(is.na(.x))))
if (any(unlist(missing_covariates) > 0)) {
  warning("Missing participant covariates remain; model sample sizes may differ. See missing_covariates.")
}
```

```{r run participant responses through toolkit}
# filter excluded/blank trials
toolkit_input_trials <- spelling_trials %>% filter(!is.na(spelling_response), spelling_response != "", !is.na(inhouse), inhouse != "")

# get toolkit pg and or probabilities of responses
pg_consistency_summary <- summarize_words(map_value(toolkit_input_trials$spelling_response, toolkit_input_trials$inhouse, "PG", all_tables_PG), "PG")
or_consistency_summary <- summarize_words(map_value(toolkit_input_trials$spelling_response, toolkit_input_trials$inhouse, "OR", all_tables_OR), "PG")

# get toolkit pg and or frequencies of responses
pg_frequency_summary <- summarize_words(map_value(toolkit_input_trials$spelling_response, toolkit_input_trials$inhouse, "PG", all_tables_PG_freq), "PG_freq")
or_frequency_summary <- summarize_words(map_value(toolkit_input_trials$spelling_response, toolkit_input_trials$inhouse, "OR", all_tables_OR_freq), "PG_freq")

# append results back to original long transcription dataframe
join_toolkit_summary <- function(data, summary_df, prefix) {
  
  toolkit_summary_unique <- summary_df %>%
    dplyr::select(spelling, pronunciation, mean, min) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(spelling, pronunciation, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      !!paste0(prefix, "_mean") := mean,
      !!paste0(prefix, "_min") := min
    )
  
  data %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      toolkit_summary_unique,
      by = c(
        "spelling_response" = "spelling",
        "inhouse" = "pronunciation"
      ),
      relationship = "many-to-one"
    )
}

spelling_trials <- spelling_trials %>%
  join_toolkit_summary(pg_consistency_summary, "pg_consistency") %>%
  join_toolkit_summary(or_consistency_summary, "or_consistency") %>%
  join_toolkit_summary(pg_frequency_summary, "pg_frequency") %>%
  join_toolkit_summary(or_frequency_summary, "or_frequency")
```

```{r helper-functions}
# Mean that returns 0 when every value in a group is NA.
# Useful for toolkit values where NA means no legal/available spelling response.
mean_or_zero <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) 0 else mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Standard mean helper for variables where an all-NA group should stay NA.
mean_ignoring_missing <- function(x) {
  mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

make_reading_skill_group <- function(x) {
  factor(
    dplyr::ntile(dplyr::desc(x), 3),
    levels = c(1, 2, 3),
    labels = c("High", "Average", "Low")
  )
}

plot_group_colors <- c(
  "High" = "deepskyblue",
  "Average" = "chartreuse3",
  "Low" = "hotpink"
)
```

```{r determine accuracy}
# top 1 and top 2 pg and or toolkit accuracy
spelling_accuracy_trials <- spelling_trials %>%
  mutate(
    pg_consistency_mean = na_if(pg_consistency_mean, 0),
    or_consistency_mean = na_if(or_consistency_mean, 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(pronunciation) %>%
  mutate(
    pg_rank = dense_rank(desc(pg_consistency_mean)),
    or_rank = dense_rank(desc(or_consistency_mean)),

    pg_top1_accuracy  = if_else(!is.na(pg_consistency_mean) & pg_rank == 1, 1L, 0L),
    or_top1_accuracy  = if_else(!is.na(or_consistency_mean) & or_rank == 1, 1L, 0L),

    pg_top2_accuracy = if_else(!is.na(pg_consistency_mean) & pg_rank <= 2, 1L, 0L),
    or_top2_accuracy = if_else(!is.na(or_consistency_mean) & or_rank <= 2, 1L, 0L)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-pg_rank, -or_rank)

# legal toolkit accuracy
spelling_accuracy_trials <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  mutate(
    pg_legal_accuracy = if_else(!is.na(pg_consistency_mean), 1L, 0L),
    or_legal_accuracy = if_else(!is.na(or_consistency_mean), 1L, 0L)
  )

# sample top 1, top 2, and legal accuracy
spelling_accuracy_trials <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  group_by(pronunciation, spelling_response) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_spelling_count = n()
  ) %>%
  group_by(pronunciation) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_spelling_probability = sample_spelling_count / n(),
    sample_rank = dense_rank(desc(sample_spelling_probability)),

    sample_top1_accuracy = as.integer(sample_rank == 1),
    sample_top2_accuracy = as.integer(sample_rank <= 2),

    sample_legal_accuracy = as.integer(sample_spelling_count > 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-sample_rank)
```

```{r compare accuracy scoring approaches}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lme4)
library(emmeans)

accuracy_comparison_trials <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  dplyr::select(
    ID,
    pronunciation,
    pg_top1_accuracy,
    or_top1_accuracy,
    sample_top1_accuracy,
    pg_top2_accuracy,
    or_top2_accuracy,
    sample_top2_accuracy,
    pg_legal_accuracy,
    or_legal_accuracy,
    sample_legal_accuracy
  ) %>%
  
  # One ID for each original participant × item response
  mutate(
    Response = interaction(ID, pronunciation, drop = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(ID, pronunciation, Response),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "accuracy"
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(
    measure_group = case_when(
      measure %in% c(
        "pg_top1_accuracy",
        "pg_top2_accuracy",
        "pg_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "PG Toolkit",

      measure %in% c(
        "or_top1_accuracy",
        "or_top2_accuracy",
        "or_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "OR Toolkit",

      measure %in% c(
        "sample_top1_accuracy",
        "sample_top2_accuracy",
        "sample_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Sample",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    measure_group = factor(
      measure_group,
      levels = c("PG Toolkit", "OR Toolkit", "Sample")
    ),

    column_label = case_when(
      measure %in% c(
        "pg_top1_accuracy",
        "or_top1_accuracy",
        "sample_top1_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Top 1",

      measure %in% c(
        "pg_top2_accuracy",
        "or_top2_accuracy",
        "sample_top2_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Top 2",

      measure %in% c(
        "pg_legal_accuracy",
        "or_legal_accuracy",
        "sample_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Legal",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    column_label = factor(
      column_label,
      levels = c("Top 1", "Top 2", "Legal")
    )
  )

model_scoring_comparison <- glmer(
  accuracy ~ measure_group * column_label +
    (1 | ID) +
    (1 | pronunciation) +
    (1 | Response),
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data = accuracy_comparison_trials,
  control = glmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
  )
)

accuracy_threshold_estimates <- emmeans(
  model_scoring_comparison,
  ~ column_label | measure_group
)

summary(accuracy_threshold_estimates, type = "response")

scoring_method_estimates <- emmeans(
  model_scoring_comparison,
  ~ measure_group | column_label
)

scoring_method_contrasts <- contrast(
  scoring_method_estimates,
  method = list(
    "PG vs OR"     = c(1, -1, 0),
    "PG vs Sample" = c(1, 0, -1),
    "OR vs Sample" = c(0, 1, -1)
  ),
  adjust = "holm"
)

summary(
  scoring_method_contrasts,
  infer = TRUE,
  type = "response"
)

summary(model_scoring_comparison)
VarCorr(model_scoring_comparison)
isSingular(model_scoring_comparison, tol = 1e-4)

#interaction contrasts
scoring_interaction_estimates <- emmeans(
  model_scoring_comparison,
  ~ measure_group * column_label)

scoring_interaction_contrasts <- contrast(
  scoring_interaction_estimates,
  interaction = list(
    column_label = list(
      "Top 1 to Top 2" = c(-1, 1, 0),
      "Top 1 to Legal" = c(-1, 0, 1),
      "Top 2 to Legal" = c(0, -1, 1)
    ),
    measure_group = list(
      "PG vs OR"     = c(1, -1, 0),
      "PG vs Sample" = c(1, 0, -1),
      "OR vs Sample" = c(0, 1, -1)
    )
  ),
  adjust = "holm"
)

summary(
  scoring_interaction_contrasts,
  infer = TRUE,
  adjust = "holm"
)
```

```{r plot comparison of scoring approaches}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# Step 1: Calculate proportion correct/incorrect for each measure
accuracy_proportions <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  dplyr::select(
    pg_top1_accuracy,
    or_top1_accuracy,
    sample_top1_accuracy,
    pg_top2_accuracy,
    or_top2_accuracy,
    sample_top2_accuracy,
    pg_legal_accuracy,
    or_legal_accuracy,
    sample_legal_accuracy
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ mean(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "column",
    values_to = "proportion_ones"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion_zeros = 1 - proportion_ones
  )

# Step 2: Reshape correct/incorrect into rows
accuracy_proportions_long <- accuracy_proportions %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(proportion_ones, proportion_zeros),
    names_to = "value_type",
    values_to = "proportion"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    value_type = recode(
      value_type,
      proportion_ones = "Correct",
      proportion_zeros = "Incorrect"
    ),
    value_type = factor(
      value_type,
      levels = c("Incorrect", "Correct")
    )
  )

# Step 3: Add measure group and scoring-definition labels
accuracy_proportions_long <- accuracy_proportions_long %>%
  mutate(
    measure_group = case_when(
      column %in% c(
        "pg_top1_accuracy",
        "pg_top2_accuracy",
        "pg_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "PG Toolkit",

      column %in% c(
        "or_top1_accuracy",
        "or_top2_accuracy",
        "or_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "OR Toolkit",

      column %in% c(
        "sample_top1_accuracy",
        "sample_top2_accuracy",
        "sample_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Sample",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    measure_group = factor(
      measure_group,
      levels = c("PG Toolkit", "OR Toolkit", "Sample")
    ),

    column_label = case_when(
      column %in% c(
        "pg_top1_accuracy",
        "or_top1_accuracy",
        "sample_top1_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Top 1",

      column %in% c(
        "pg_top2_accuracy",
        "or_top2_accuracy",
        "sample_top2_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Top 2",

      column %in% c(
        "pg_legal_accuracy",
        "or_legal_accuracy",
        "sample_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Legal",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    column_label = factor(
      column_label,
      levels = c("Top 1", "Top 2", "Legal")
    )
  )

# Step 4: Plot
plot_accuracy_by_scoring_method <- ggplot(
  accuracy_proportions_long,
  aes(
    x = column_label,
    y = proportion,
    fill = value_type
  )
) +
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity",
    position = "stack",
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Spelling Accuracy by Measure",
    x = "Accuracy Threshold",
    y = "Proportion of Spelling Accuracy",
    fill = "Accuracy"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("hotpink", "chartreuse3")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    . ~ measure_group,
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 16
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    )
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(
      accuracy_proportions_long,
      value_type == "Correct"
    ),
    aes(
      label = scales::percent(
        proportion,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    ),
    vjust = -0.5,
    color = "black",
    size = 5
  )

print(plot_accuracy_by_scoring_method)

ggsave(
  "plot_acc.png",
  plot = plot_accuracy_by_scoring_method,
  width = 10,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
# Calculate the average for each subject
participant_spelling_summary <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarise(
    age = mean(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
    education = mean(Education, na.rm = TRUE),
    WRMT_BSC = mean(WRMT_BSC, na.rm = TRUE),
    WRMT_WID = mean(WRMT_WID, na.rm = TRUE),
    WRMT_WA = mean(WRMT_WA, na.rm = TRUE),
    WJTA_SPELL = mean(WJTA_SPELL, na.rm = TRUE),
    length_avg = mean(length, na.rm = TRUE),
    sample_prob_avg = mean(sample_spelling_probability, na.rm = TRUE),
    pg_consistency_min_participant_mean = mean(pg_consistency_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    or_consistency_min_participant_mean = mean(or_consistency_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    pg_frequency_min_participant_mean = mean(pg_frequency_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    or_frequency_min_participant_mean = mean(or_frequency_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    pg_consistency_mean_participant_mean = mean(pg_consistency_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    or_consistency_mean_participant_mean = mean(or_consistency_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    pg_frequency_mean_participant_mean = mean(pg_frequency_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    or_frequency_mean_participant_mean = mean(or_frequency_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    pg_top1_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(pg_top1_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    pg_top2_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(pg_top2_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    or_top1_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(or_top1_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    or_top2_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(or_top2_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    sample_top1_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(sample_top1_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    sample_top2_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(sample_top2_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    pg_legal_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(pg_legal_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    or_legal_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(or_legal_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
    sample_legal_accuracy_participant_mean = mean(sample_legal_accuracy, na.rm = TRUE))

participant_spelling_summary <- participant_spelling_summary %>%
  mutate(reading_skill_group = ntile(desc(WRMT_WID), 3))

# Calculate the average for each subject with zero coding
spelling_accuracy_zero_coded <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      c(pg_consistency_mean, or_consistency_mean, pg_frequency_mean, or_frequency_mean, pg_consistency_min, or_consistency_min, pg_frequency_min, or_frequency_min),
      ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0)
    )
  )

participant_spelling_summary_zero_coded <- spelling_accuracy_zero_coded %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarise(
    age = mean(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
    education = mean(Education, na.rm = TRUE),
    WRMT_BSC = mean(WRMT_BSC, na.rm = TRUE),
    WRMT_WID = mean(WRMT_WID, na.rm = TRUE),
    WRMT_WA = mean(WRMT_WA, na.rm = TRUE),
    WJTA_SPELL = mean(WJTA_SPELL, na.rm = TRUE),
```

```{r how does literacy skill predict spelling accuracy variously defined?}
accuracy_p_values <- map_dfr(
  names(accuracy_models),
  function(model_name) {
    
    coef_table <- summary(accuracy_models[[model_name]])$coefficients
    
    tibble(
      model = model_name,
      predictor = accuracy_predictors,
      p = coef_table[accuracy_predictors, "Pr(>|z|)"]
    )
  }
)

  mutate(
    q = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr")
  ) %>%
  ungroup())
```

## Spelling agreement and variability
```{r predict entropy from reading group}
calculate_entropy <- function(counts) {
  probabilities <- counts / sum(counts)
  -sum(probabilities * log(probabilities, base = 2))
}

calculate_entropy <- function(counts) {
  p <- counts / sum(counts)
  -sum(p * log2(p))
}

# Add reading-skill group and pronunciation count
participant_reading_groups <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  distinct(ID, WRMT_WID) %>%
  mutate(
    reading_skill_group = factor(
      ntile(desc(WRMT_WID), 3),
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c("High", "Average", "Low")))

spelling_agreement_trials <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  select(-any_of("reading_skill_group")) %>%
  left_join(participant_reading_groups, by = c("ID", "WRMT_WID"))

# Calculate spelling entropy by pronunciation and reading group
item_group_entropy <- spelling_agreement_trials %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(reading_skill_group),
    !is.na(pronunciation),
    !is.na(spelling_response)
  ) %>%
  count(reading_skill_group, pronunciation, spelling_response, name = "spelling_count") %>%
  group_by(reading_skill_group, pronunciation) %>%
  summarise(
    spelling_entropy = calculate_entropy(spelling_count),
    length = nchar(first(pronunciation)),
    n_trials = sum(spelling_count),
    .groups = "drop")

# Add entropy back to trial-level data
spelling_agreement_trials <- spelling_agreement_trials %>%
  left_join(item_group_entropy %>%
      select(reading_skill_group, pronunciation, spelling_entropy), by = c("reading_skill_group", "pronunciation"))

# Mixed-effects model
summary(
  model_entropy_by_reading_group <- lmer(
    spelling_entropy ~ reading_skill_group +
    length +
    (1 | pronunciation),
    data = item_group_entropy
  )
)

anova(model_entropy_by_reading_group)

library(emmeans)
emmeans(model_entropy_by_reading_group, pairwise ~ reading_skill_group, adjust = "tukey")

# Plot-ready dataset
item_group_entropy_plot_data <- item_group_entropy %>% filter(!is.na(spelling_entropy)) %>%
  mutate(pronunciation = reorder(pronunciation, spelling_entropy))

print(plot_entropy <- ggplot(item_group_entropy_plot_data,
  aes(x = pronunciation, y = spelling_entropy, color = reading_skill_group)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(group = reading_skill_group),
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = plot_group_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Spelling Entropy for Each Item by Reading Group",
    x = "Pseudoword Item",
    y = "Mean Spelling Entropy",
    color = "Group") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0.5,
      size = 20,
      face = "bold"),
    legend.position = c(0.98, 0.30),
    legend.justification = c(1, 1),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16)))

ggsave("plot_entropy.png", plot = plot_entropy, width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r predict idiosyncratic responses from reading group}
# Idiosyncratic trial flag:
# spelling occurs only once for a given pronunciation across the full sample
idiosyncratic_spelling_trials <- spelling_agreement_trials %>%
  filter(!is.na(pronunciation), !is.na(spelling_response)) %>%
  add_count(pronunciation, spelling_response, name = "n_in_sample") %>%
  mutate(
    idiosyncratic_trial = n_in_sample == 1,
    reading_skill_group = factor(
      reading_skill_group,
      levels = c("High", "Average", "Low")))

# Participant-level idiosyncratic counts/rates
participant_idiosyncrasy <- idiosyncratic_spelling_trials %>%
  filter(!is.na(reading_skill_group)) %>%
  group_by(ID, reading_skill_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    n_idiosyncratic_trials = sum(idiosyncratic_trial),
    prop_idiosyncratic = mean(idiosyncratic_trial),
    .groups = "drop")

# Item-level idiosyncratic counts for plotting
item_group_idiosyncrasy <- idiosyncratic_spelling_trials %>%
  filter(!is.na(reading_skill_group)) %>%
  group_by(reading_skill_group, pronunciation) %>%
  summarise(
    n_idio = sum(idiosyncratic_trial),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pronunciation = reorder(
      pronunciation,
      n_idio,
      FUN = mean
    ),
    reading_skill_group = factor(
      reading_skill_group,
      levels = c("Low", "Average", "High")
    )
  )

# Unique spelling counts by pronunciation × reading group
item_group_unique_spellings <- spelling_agreement_trials %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(pronunciation),
    !is.na(reading_skill_group),
    !is.na(spelling_response)
  ) %>%
  group_by(pronunciation, reading_skill_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_unique_spellings = n_distinct(spelling_response),
    length = nchar(first(pronunciation)),
    n_trials = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pronunciation = reorder(
      pronunciation,
      n_unique_spellings,
      FUN = mean
    ),
    reading_skill_group = factor(
      reading_skill_group,
      levels = c("Low", "Average", "High")))

# Poisson mixed-effects model
summary(
  model_unique_spellings_by_reading_group <- glmer(
    n_unique_spellings ~ reading_skill_group +
    offset(log(n_trials)) +
    length +
    (1 | pronunciation),
    family = poisson,
    data = item_group_unique_spellings
  )
)

drop1(model_unique_spellings_by_reading_group, test = "Chisq")

emmeans(model_unique_spellings_by_reading_group, pairwise ~ reading_skill_group, adjust = "tukey")

print(plot_unique_spellings_by_reading_group <- ggplot(
  item_group_unique_spellings,
  aes(x = pronunciation, y = n_unique_spellings, color = reading_skill_group)
) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, aes(group = reading_skill_group), linetype = "solid") +
  scale_color_manual(values = plot_group_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Idiosyncratic Spellings for Each Item by Reading Group",
    x = "Pseudoword Item",
    y = "Number of Idiosyncratic Spellings",
    color = "Group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 20, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = c(0.20, 0.90),
    legend.justification = c(1, 1),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16)
  ))

library(patchwork)

print(plot_agreement_combined <- plot_entropy / plot_unique_spellings_by_reading_group +
```

## Supplementary analyses
```{r}
sample_accuracy_lookup <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  distinct(pronunciation, spelling_response, sample_spelling_probability) %>%
  group_by(pronunciation) %>%
  arrange(desc(sample_spelling_probability), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_cum_prob_before = lag(cumsum(sample_spelling_probability), default = 0),

    sample_top25_accuracy = if_else(sample_cum_prob_before < 0.25, 1L, 0L),
    sample_top50_accuracy = if_else(sample_cum_prob_before < 0.50, 1L, 0L),
    sample_top75_accuracy = if_else(sample_cum_prob_before < 0.75, 1L, 0L)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

cumulative_accuracy_trials <- spelling_accuracy_trials %>%
  left_join(
    sample_accuracy_lookup,
    by = c("pronunciation", "spelling_response", "sample_spelling_probability")
  )
```

```{r cumulative sample models}
summary(
  model_accuracy_sample_top25 <- glmer(
    sample_top25_accuracy ~ word_reading_standardized +
    pseudoword_reading_standardized +

    age_standardized +
    education_standardized +
    stimulus_length_standardized +

  )
)

summary(
  model_accuracy_sample_top50 <- glmer(
    sample_top50_accuracy ~ word_reading_standardized +

    (1 | pronunciation) +
    (1 | ID),
    data = cumulative_accuracy_standardized,
    family = binomial
  )
)

summary(
  model_accuracy_sample_top75 <- glmer(
    sample_top75_accuracy ~ word_reading_standardized +
    pseudoword_reading_standardized +
    word_spelling_standardized +
    age_standardized +
    education_standardized +
    stimulus_length_standardized +
    (1 | pronunciation) +
    (1 | ID),
    data = cumulative_accuracy_standardized,
    family = binomial
  )
)

# fdr correction
cumulative_accuracy_models <- list(
  Top25 = model_accuracy_sample_top25,
  Top50 = model_accuracy_sample_top50,
  Top75 = model_accuracy_sample_top75,
  Legal = model_accuracy_sample_legal
)

cumulative_accuracy_predictors <- c("word_reading_standardized", "pseudoword_reading_standardized", "word_spelling_standardized", "age_standardized", "education_standardized", "stimulus_length_standardized")

cumulative_accuracy_p_values <- map_dfr(
  names(cumulative_accuracy_models),
  function(model_name) {
    
    coef_table <- summary(cumulative_accuracy_models[[model_name]])$coefficients
    
    tibble(
      model = model_name,
      predictor = cumulative_accuracy_predictors,
      p = coef_table[cumulative_accuracy_predictors, "Pr(>|z|)"]
    )
  }
)

print(cumulative_accuracy_p_values <- cumulative_accuracy_p_values %>%
  group_by(predictor) %>%
  mutate(
    q = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr")
  ) %>%
  ungroup())

library(performance)
lapply(cumulative_accuracy_models, r2)

print(cumulative_accuracy_r_squared <- data.frame(
  Model = names(cumulative_accuracy_models),
  Marginal_R2 = sapply(
    cumulative_accuracy_models,
    function(m) r2(m)$R2_marginal
  ),
  Conditional_R2 = sapply(
    cumulative_accuracy_models,
    function(m) r2(m)$R2_conditional
  )))
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# Step 1: Calculate proportion correct/incorrect for each measure
all_accuracy_proportions <- cumulative_accuracy_trials %>%
  dplyr::select(
    # PG Toolkit
    pg_top1_accuracy,
    pg_top2_accuracy,
    pg_legal_accuracy,

    # OR Toolkit
    or_top1_accuracy,
    or_top2_accuracy,
    or_legal_accuracy,

    # Sample
    sample_top1_accuracy,
    sample_top2_accuracy,
    sample_top25_accuracy,
    sample_top50_accuracy,
    sample_top75_accuracy,
    sample_legal_accuracy
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ mean(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "column",
    values_to = "proportion_ones"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion_zeros = 1 - proportion_ones
  )

# Duplicate PG and OR Legal rows for the "no position" bars
all_accuracy_proportions <- bind_rows(
  all_accuracy_proportions,

  all_accuracy_proportions %>%
    filter(column == "pg_legal_accuracy") %>%
    mutate(column = "legalpg_acc_noposition"),

  all_accuracy_proportions %>%
    filter(column == "or_legal_accuracy") %>%
    mutate(column = "legalor_acc_noposition")
)

# Step 2: Reshape correct/incorrect into rows
all_accuracy_proportions_long <- all_accuracy_proportions %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(proportion_ones, proportion_zeros),
    names_to = "value_type",
    values_to = "proportion"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    value_type = recode(
      value_type,
      proportion_ones = "Correct",
      proportion_zeros = "Incorrect"
    ),
    value_type = factor(
      value_type,
      levels = c("Incorrect", "Correct")
    )
  )

# Step 3: Add measure group and scoring-definition labels
# Step 3: Add measure group and scoring-definition labels

all_accuracy_proportions_long <- all_accuracy_proportions_long %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Assign each accuracy measure to a group
    measure_group = case_when(
      
      column %in% c(
        "pg_top1_accuracy",
        "pg_top2_accuracy",
        "pg_legal_accuracy",
        "legalpg_acc_noposition"
      ) ~ "PG Toolkit",
      
      column %in% c(
        "or_top1_accuracy",
        "or_top2_accuracy",
        "or_legal_accuracy",
        "legalor_acc_noposition"
      ) ~ "OR Toolkit",
      
      column %in% c(
        "sample_top1_accuracy",
        "sample_top2_accuracy",
        "sample_top25_accuracy",
        "sample_top50_accuracy",
        "sample_top75_accuracy",
        "sample_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Sample",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    # Set facet order
    measure_group = factor(
      measure_group,
      levels = c(
        "PG Toolkit",
        "OR Toolkit",
        "Sample"
      )
    ),
    
    # Create labels for each scoring definition
    column_label = case_when(
      
      column %in% c(
        "pg_top1_accuracy",
        "or_top1_accuracy",
        "sample_top1_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Top 1",
      
      column %in% c(
        "pg_top2_accuracy",
        "or_top2_accuracy",
        "sample_top2_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Top 2",
      
      column == "sample_top25_accuracy" ~ "Top 25%",
      column == "sample_top50_accuracy" ~ "Top 50%",
      column == "sample_top75_accuracy" ~ "Top 75%",
      
      column %in% c(
        "pg_legal_accuracy",
        "or_legal_accuracy"
      ) ~ "Legal (Positional)",
      
      column %in% c(
        "legalpg_acc_noposition",
        "legalor_acc_noposition"
      ) ~ "Legal (Non-Positional)",
      
      column == "sample_legal_accuracy" ~ "Legal",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    # Set order of scoring definitions
    column_label = factor(
      column_label,
      levels = c(
        "Top 1",
        "Top 2",
        "Top 25%",
        "Top 50%",
        "Top 75%",
        "Legal",
        "Legal (Positional)",
        "Legal (Non-Positional)"
      )
    )
  )


# Step 4: Plot

plot_accuracy_all_definitions <- ggplot(
  all_accuracy_proportions_long,
  aes(
    x = column_label,
    y = proportion,
    fill = value_type
  )
) +
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity",
    position = "stack",
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Spelling Accuracy by Measure",
    x = "Accuracy Threshold",
    y = "Proportion of Spelling Accuracy",
    fill = "Accuracy"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Incorrect" = "hotpink",
      "Correct" = "chartreuse3"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    . ~ measure_group,
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(
      all_accuracy_proportions_long,
      value_type == "Correct"
    ),
    aes(
      label = scales::percent(
        proportion,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    ),
    vjust = -0.5,
    color = "black",
    size = 5
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 16
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 16
    ),
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 16
    ),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 16
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 16
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 16
    ),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    )
  )

print(plot_accuracy_all_definitions)


# Save plot

ggsave(
  "plot_acc_all.png",
  plot = plot_accuracy_all_definitions,
  width = 14,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r correlation between all predictor variables for models}
library(dplyr)
library(ppcor)

participant_correlation_variables <- participant_spelling_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(
    WRMT_WID, WRMT_WA, WJTA_SPELL, age, education,
    pg_consistency_mean_participant_mean, or_consistency_mean_participant_mean,
    pg_frequency_mean_participant_mean, or_frequency_mean_participant_mean
  )

participant_correlation_complete <- participant_correlation_variables %>%
  tidyr::drop_na() %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    "WRMT Word ID"        = WRMT_WID,
    "WRMT Word Attack"   = WRMT_WA,
    "WJTA Spelling"= WJTA_SPELL,
    "Age"    = age,
    "Education"    = education,
    "PG Consistency" = pg_consistency_mean_participant_mean,
    "OR Consistency" = or_consistency_mean_participant_mean,
    "PG Frequency"   = pg_frequency_mean_participant_mean,
    "OR Frequency"   = or_frequency_mean_participant_mean
  )


pearson_correlation_matrix <- cor(participant_correlation_complete, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
round(pearson_correlation_matrix, 3)

# If you want Spearman (robust to nonlinearity / ranks)
spearman_correlation_matrix <- cor(participant_correlation_complete, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")
round(spearman_correlation_matrix, 3)

# Partial correlations controlling for Education and WRMT_WA
partial_correlations_all_variables <- ppcor::pcor(participant_correlation_complete, method = "pearson")  # all partialled against the rest
round(partial_correlations_all_variables$estimate, 3)
round(partial_correlations_all_variables$p.value, 3)

toolkit_correlation_variables <- participant_correlation_complete %>%
  dplyr::select(
   "PG Consistency", "OR Consistency", "PG Frequency", "OR Frequency", "Education", "WJTA Spelling", "WRMT Word Attack"
  )

partial_correlations_toolkit <- ppcor::pcor(toolkit_correlation_variables, method = "pearson")
round(partial_correlations_toolkit$estimate, 3)

library(reshape2)
library(ggplot2)

correlation_plot_data <- melt(round(pearson_correlation_matrix, 2))

# Keep only upper triangle to avoid mirrored side
correlation_plot_upper_triangle <- correlation_plot_data %>%
  filter(as.numeric(Var1) < as.numeric(Var2))

print(plot_participant_correlations <- ggplot(correlation_plot_upper_triangle, aes(Var2, Var1, fill = value)) +   # swap Var1 and Var2
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = value)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low="deepskyblue", mid="white", high="hotpink",
                       midpoint=0, limits=c(-1,1)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size=14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x="", y="", fill="r"))

ggsave("ntr_pw_spell_corrmat.png", plot = plot_participant_correlations, width = 8, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

```{r partial correlation plots}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

# Remove rows where ID is "NTR0265"
participant_spelling_summary_filtered <- participant_spelling_summary %>%
  filter(!ID %in% c("NTR0265", "NTR0427"))



# ----------------------------
# 1. Start with participant-level dataframe
# ----------------------------
participant_residualized_measures <- participant_spelling_summary %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    pg_consistency = pg_consistency_mean_participant_mean,
    or_consistency = or_consistency_mean_participant_mean,
    pg_frequency = pg_frequency_mean_participant_mean,
    or_frequency = or_frequency_mean_participant_mean
  ) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(
    pg_consistency,
    or_consistency,
    pg_frequency,
    or_frequency,
    education,
    age,
    WRMT_WA,
    WJTA_SPELL,
    WRMT_WID,
    reading_skill_group
  )

# ----------------------------
# 2. Residualize each DV for covariates
#    WRMT_WID is intentionally NOT included
# ----------------------------
participant_residualized_measures <- participant_residualized_measures %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    PG_Cons_resid = resid(
      lm(pg_consistency ~ education + age, data = .)
    ),
    
    OR_Cons_resid = resid(
      lm(or_consistency ~ education + age, data = .)
    ),
    
    PG_Freq_resid = resid(
      lm(pg_frequency ~ education + age, data = .)
    ),
    
    OR_Freq_resid = resid(
      lm(or_frequency ~ education + age, data = .)
    )
  )

# ----------------------------
# 3. Reshape to long format
# ----------------------------
partial_plot_measures_long <- participant_residualized_measures %>%
  dplyr::select(
    ID,
    reading_skill_group,
    WRMT_WA,
    PG_Cons_resid,
    OR_Cons_resid,
    PG_Freq_resid,
    OR_Freq_resid
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      PG_Cons_resid,
      OR_Cons_resid,
      PG_Freq_resid,
      OR_Freq_resid
    ),
    names_to = "Measure",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Measure = factor(
      Measure,
      levels = c(
        "PG_Cons_resid",
        "OR_Cons_resid",
        "PG_Freq_resid",
        "OR_Freq_resid"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Mean PG Consistency",
        "Mean OR Consistency",
        "Mean PG Frequency",
        "Mean OR Frequency"
      )
    ),
    
    reading_skill_group = factor(
      reading_skill_group,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c("High", "Average", "Low")
    )
  )

partial_plot_correlations <- partial_plot_measures_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Measure) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    test = list(stats::cor.test(WRMT_WA, Value, method = "pearson")),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    r = purrr::map_dbl(test, ~ unname(.x$estimate)),
    p = purrr::map_dbl(test, ~ .x$p.value),
    label = paste0(
      "r = ", sprintf("%.2f", r),
      "\n",
      "p ", dplyr::if_else(
        p < .001,
        "< .001",
        paste0("= ", sprintf("%.3f", p))
      )
    )
  )

# ----------------------------
# 4. Plot
# ----------------------------
print(plot_partial_word_attack <- ggplot(
  partial_plot_measures_long,
  aes(x = WRMT_WA, y = Value, color = reading_skill_group)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  
  geom_smooth(
    aes(group = 1),
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE,
    color = "gray40"
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    data = partial_plot_correlations,
    aes(
      x = Inf,
      y = -Inf,
      label = label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 1.1,
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 5
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(~ Measure, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "High" = "deepskyblue",
      "Average" = "chartreuse3",
      "Low" = "hotpink"
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Word Attack Score",
    y = "Residualized Toolkit Measure",
    color = "Reading Skill Group",
    title = "Relationship Between Pseudoword Reading Skill and Mean Toolkit Measures (Illegal = NA)"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0.5,
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines")
  ))

ggsave("plot_partial_legal_WA.png", plot = plot_partial_word_attack, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```
